private_lines.Chloe: You live in Chorlton with a flatmate and work in the accounts team, mostly on month-end reporting. This week you have a client review on Wednesday and are trying to finish the management pack before the weekend.
private_lines.Dev: You live in Didsbury with your partner and two teenagers, and you have been in accounts for over twenty years. This week you are catching up after a busy close, and your eldest has a school concert on Thursday evening.
private_lines.Hannah: You rent a flat in Fallowfield with two friends and work in the accounts team, mainly on accounts payable. This week you are doing a short course on evenings and trying to keep up with the weekly tasks.
private_lines.Tom: You live in Stockport with your wife and have worked in the firm's accounts team for nearly twenty years. This week you are on bank reconciliations and have a dentist appointment on Tuesday morning.

setting: You all work in a small accounts team at a firm in Manchester and share a group chat for day-to-day office matters. You know each other from the office, and the chat has been active for months. Dev keeps the supplier invoices spreadsheet that the team needs for month-end, and Chloe needs it by the end of Friday 27 November. Last week the chat was about who was bringing biscuits to the Thursday meeting.

Chloe.who: 31, woman, team-mate who needs the spreadsheet
Chloe.knows: You sit two desks from Dev and know he holds the supplier sheet. Hannah is the newest in the team and quick to reply. Tom has been there longest and handles the bank reconciliations.
Chloe.texts: You message the group now and then, mostly when you need something from someone, and you keep messages short and mostly lowercase. You use the odd emoji and rarely punctuate heavily.
ex: anyone know if the kettle's been fixed yet
biscuits on thursday, who's sorted them
can you grab the good coffee if you're in tomorrow
ta
going to lunch at 1, shout if you want to come
did tom ever reply about the room booking

Dev.who: 45, man, team-mate who holds the spreadsheet
Dev.knows: Chloe sits nearby and has been chasing the month-end figures. Hannah joined a few months ago and you have been training her on the ledgers. Tom has been in the team for years and you often check numbers with him.
Dev.texts: You message the group occasionally, usually to answer a question or confirm something, and your messages are fairly full sentences with normal capitals and full stops. You rarely use emoji and sometimes add a thumbs up.
ex: Yes, I'll be in by nine.
Biscuits are sorted, Hannah's bringing them.
Thursday's fine with me.
Can someone remind me which room we booked?
Cheers Tom, that helps.
I'm out Wednesday afternoon, so message me before then.

Hannah.knows: Dev has been patient about teaching you the ledgers. Chloe is someone you ask when you're unsure about the month-end timings. Tom is friendly and often joins your lunch trips.
Hannah.texts: You message the group fairly often, including small things and jokes, and you use plenty of emoji, exclamation marks and lowercase. Your messages are usually short, though sometimes you send a few in a row.
ex: omg it's so cold today 🥶
anyone want a coffee from the place downstairs??
ha yes tom that's the one 😂
does the printer on 3 work or is it just me
heading off early, see you all tmrw!
who's coming to the quiz on friday 🙈

Tom.knows: Chloe is sharp and always well prepared for reviews. Dev has been a steady presence for years and is the one you check figures with. Hannah is energetic and fits in well with the team.
Tom.texts: You message the group only when you have something to add, and your messages are short and plain with normal punctuation. You rarely use emoji and do not use abbreviations.
ex: Lunch at one for anyone interested.
Rain's coming in this afternoon, bring a coat.
Thanks, I'll sort the room.
Can someone let reception know I'm in late tomorrow?
Not sure about Thursday, let me check my diary.
Good to see the new coffee machine's working.

situation: You work together in a small accounts team.
topic: You need Dev's spreadsheet of supplier invoices before the end of Friday.
